newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court bars Canadian group from B Band bids.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court bars Canadian group from B Band bids.

text.p: A consortium including BCE's Bell Canada and TIW International was barred from bidding for two cellular telephone concessions in Brazil by a high court ruling Friday, a court spokesman said.

A judge at the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ) ruled in the government's favor by crushing an injunction which had allowed the consortium called Telet to continue bidding for the concessions, despite being disqualified by the Communications Ministry.
"The injunction was overruled and Telet cannot bid for the concessions," the spokesman said.
The ruling is the latest twist in an increasingly public dispute between the Telet group and Communications Minister Sergio Motta.

Motta ruled in June that Telet could not take part in bids for concessions to provide B Band cellular services in three regions which encompassing Sao Paulo city, Sao Paulo state and Rio de Janeiro state.

Telet then won an injunction that allowed it to continue in the bidding process, pending a future ruling on the merit of its appeal. Although a group including Bellsouth Corp. won the Sao Paulo city concession earlier this month, Telet had remained in the running for the other two concessions.
Officials from the Telet group complained they were unfairly disqualifed by the minister, despite having been earlier approved for participation in bidding process by a ministry committee.
In a statement, the STJ said the judge agreed with the government's argument that Telet lacked technical experience to handle the three big contracts.

Telet remain in the bidding process for three smaller concessions. Another group, Americel, which comprises the same members as Telet, has already been awarded a B Band concession for a region in central-western Brazil which includes Brasilia.
